VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
Quality & Regulatory Affairs

MEMORANDUM

Date: October 15, 2019
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: ApexHip Design History File / Risk Management File
Subject: Risk Management File Update — ApexHip Wear/Edge-Loading Risk

Per Dana Okonkwo's request following the September regulatory review, this memo documents an update to the ApexHip risk management file (RMF-APX-002) to incorporate findings related to edge-loading wear at high cup inclination angles.

Background

The original ApexHip design inputs (approved September 2015) and associated FMEA (DR-1 through DR-3, 2015–2016) identified wear debris generation as a known hazard for metal-on-metal bearing surfaces, with mitigation via material selection (Co/Cr per ASTM F1537) and surface finish controls. Per procedure, the DR-3 design review (November 2016) established the wear-test protocol per ISO 14242, and the team elected to test at the standard 45-degree cup inclination angle only. This was consistent with predicate testing practice at the time and was not flagged as a deviation requiring additional risk analysis.

New Information — 2019 Retest

In February 2019, Tom Halvorsen's team re-ran wear testing at 55 degrees of inclination, a configuration more representative of higher-inclination cup placements observed clinically. Results showed a 4–6x increase in volumetric wear compared to the 45-degree baseline. Meridian Testing Labs independently confirmed elevated wear rates under the higher-inclination protocol (report attached to DHF, ref. Meridian-2019-0311). This constitutes new information not considered in the original FMEA and warrants a formal update to the risk file per our design control procedures.

Risk Analysis Update

The edge-loading wear hazard has been added to the RMF as Hazard ID H-014, with the following updated ratings:

Hazard: Elevated wear at high cup inclination (edge loading)
Severity: 4 (Serious — potential for ARMD, revision surgery)
Pre-mitigation Occurrence: 3 (Occasional, dependent on surgical placement)
Pre-mitigation Risk Index: Unacceptable, requires mitigation

Mitigation implemented: Update to surgical technique guide emphasizing target cup inclination of 40–45 degrees; surgeon training materials revised; Dear Doctor communication under consideration by RA (separate track).

Post-mitigation Occurrence: 2 (Remote, assuming compliance with revised technique guidance)
Post-mitigation Risk Index: Acceptable, subject to PMS monitoring

A design change, ECO-2019-118, was proposed by Engineering to address the underlying wear mechanism (candidate approaches include head/cup clearance revision and alternative bearing surface). This ECO remains open. Per discussion with Halvorsen, Raman, and Mendes, the ECO has been deferred pending further data collection, as the surgical-technique mitigation is judged sufficient to bring residual risk to an acceptable level in the interim.

Conclusion

Based on the mitigation described above, residual risk associated with the edge-loading wear hazard is assessed as acceptable, consistent with our risk acceptability criteria (RMF-APX-002, Section 6). This determination is conditioned on continued monitoring of complaint trending, MDR data, and registry signals for any indication that the surgical-technique mitigation is not achieving the intended reduction in occurrence. Complaint Handling will continue to track ApexHip revision-related complaints on a quarterly basis and will escalate to Design Assurance if trends deviate from expectations.

This RMF update has been entered into the DHF index under ApexHip, Risk Management, Rev. C.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
INTERNAL MEMORANDUM — CLINICAL

Date: January 18, 2024
From: Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer
To: Rob Castellano; Owen Park; Dana Okonkwo
Subject: Clinical rationale for ApexHip market action

This memo summarizes the clinical basis supporting my recommendation that Veridian proceed to a full voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip, rather than pursue a further labeling revision.

Background. The March 2021 NJR annual report identified a 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for ApexHip, against a class average of 3.2% for metal-on-metal and comparable large-head hip systems. This is more than double the expected benchmark and, notably, is consistent in direction (though not identical in magnitude) with AJRR figures received in late 2021. Both registries point to the same underlying mechanism: edge-loading wear at higher cup inclination angles producing elevated Co/Cr ion levels and, in a subset of patients, adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD) — pseudotumor formation and periprosthetic tissue necrosis requiring revision.

We responded to the September 2021 signal review with a label update and an October 2021 Dear Doctor letter emphasizing precise cup positioning and post-op ion monitoring. I supported that step at the time as a reasonable interim measure. However, complaint and MDR data since then have not shown the improvement we hoped for. Revision-related ARMD reports have continued at a rate inconsistent with a labeling-driven fix — surgeons are, by and large, following the positioning guidance, and we are still seeing early revisions in patients implanted well after the letter went out. That tells me this is not principally a technique issue that can be trained around; it is a design/wear characteristic of the bearing surface at the inclination angles surgeons actually achieve in practice.

I want to be explicit about a separate matter so it is not conflated in any external communication. The June 2022 recall of cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 addressed a KinetiCoat adhesion defect traced to a plasma-spray parameter drift at the Cork facility. That is a discrete manufacturing quality issue, confined to a defined lot range and time window, and it is mechanically unrelated to the wear/ion signal described above, which is present across lots and predates the affected manufacturing period. I recognize plaintiffs' counsel may attempt to present these as a single storyline of "ApexHip failure," and I'd urge that our public materials, regulatory filings, and any physician communications keep the two issues clearly delineated — both because it is clinically accurate and because collapsing them risks overstating the scope of the coating problem while understating the seriousness of the wear signal.

Recommendation. Given the persistence of the ARMD/revision signal after a labeling intervention, and the magnitude of the registry gap versus class average, I do not believe an additional label change will meaningfully change patient outcomes. I recommend Veridian proceed with a full, voluntary withdrawal of ApexHip from the market, with appropriate physician notification regarding ongoing monitoring of implanted patients.

Happy to discuss further before this goes to the board.

Leon

meta.gray_rationale: The memo distinguishes the coating recall from the wear issue but discusses both, so a reviewer could include or exclude it from the narrow recall RFP depending on how strictly they read scope.

Re: Response to Form FDA 483 Observations dated June 25, 2021

Dear Investigator Delgado:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. submits this response to the three observations listed on Form FDA 483 issued at the close of the June 2021 inspection of our Warsaw, Indiana facility. We take these observations seriously and have initiated corrective actions to strengthen the timeliness, consistency, and documentation of our complaint-handling and Medical Device Reporting processes.

1. Complaint record documentation and review timeliness

The observation identified instances in which complaint records did not contain sufficiently contemporaneous documentation of intake review, follow-up activity, or closure rationale as required under 21 CFR 820.198. Effective July 12, 2021, Quality has implemented an interim daily review of newly entered and aging complaint records by the Complaint Handling Supervisor. A revised complaint-handling work instruction, QP-198-04, is being finalized and will require documented review milestones, escalation of overdue follow-up, and defined closure approval criteria.

All personnel assigned complaint intake, investigation, or closure responsibilities will complete retraining on the revised procedure by August 31, 2021. Training completion will be tracked through the company learning-management system and effectiveness will be assessed through a 30-day sample audit.

2. Complaint trending and escalation

The observation further noted that our existing process did not consistently document timely escalation of potentially reportable complaint trends. Veridian is revising its complaint trending procedure to require monthly cross-functional review of complaint categories, including clinical outcomes and product-performance allegations, with participation from Quality, Regulatory Affairs, and Post-Market Surveillance.

In addition, TrackWise configuration changes are underway to provide automated aging alerts at 15, 30, and 45 days for open complaint records and to identify records pending MDR assessment. The TrackWise aging-alert function is targeted to be live no later than September 30, 2021. Until implementation is complete, Quality will distribute a weekly manual aging report to the responsible managers and Regulatory Affairs.

3. Medical Device Reporting assessment

The inspection identified instances where the basis for MDR reportability decisions was not documented with sufficient specificity under 21 CFR Part 803. Veridian has issued interim guidance requiring Regulatory Affairs review of all complaints alleging revision surgery, elevated metal-ion results, adverse local tissue reaction, infection requiring intervention, or other serious injury potentially associated with an ApexHip device.

We will conduct a retrospective audit of ApexHip complaint files received from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2020 to confirm MDR reportability assessments and supporting documentation. The audit will begin August 2, 2021 and is targeted for completion by October 29, 2021. Any newly identified reportable events will be submitted in accordance with the applicable requirements of 21 CFR 803, including the reporting timeframes prescribed by 21 CFR 803.50.

These corrective actions are intended to address administrative and procedural timeliness gaps. They do not reflect a determination that ApexHip, or any other Veridian product, has a product defect. We will provide status updates and supporting documentation as corrective actions are completed.

Please contact me if additional information would be helpful.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo

Dana,

Per your request, I evaluated our reporting posture under 21 CFR Part 803 regarding the NJR data.

In short, registry trend data alone typically does not create a standalone reportability trigger under 21 CFR 803.50. Individual MDRs are being filed per complaint per procedure as adverse events and revisions are confirmed through TrackWise. FDA guidance consistently frames 803 reporting obligations around discrete events (death, serious injury, or malfunction that would likely cause either if recurred) rather than aggregate external population metrics.

However, given that Investigator Delgado's inspection is imminent, I strongly recommend documenting our formal clinical and technical review of the registry dataset directly within our internal PMS files. If the agency inquires into how we monitor post-market signals alongside our complaint trends, having that documented assessment ready will demonstrate appropriate oversight under 820.198.

PURPOSE OF MEETING:
To review investigative findings, finalize procedural determinations, and formally close Case ETH-2021-11-042, initially received via the Veridian EthicsPoint hotline on November 18, 2021.

BACKGROUND & DELAY SUMMARY:
The intake report alleged that members of the Quality and Complaint Handling group engaged in the intentional suppression, delay, and reclassification of post-market complaint trends to avoid crossing internal statistical alert thresholds in TrackWise. The matter specifically involved complaint categorization criteria for adverse tissue reactions and cobalt-chromium wear debris.

Lisa Tran noted for the record that while intake occurred in late 2021, the comprehensive conclusion of this review was substantially delayed (spanning approximately 21 months). This extended timeline resulted from the implementation of the company-wide litigation hold issued in February 2022, external counsel document preservation protocols, and the subsequent prioritization of data-collection requests related to outside product liability inquiries.

FINDINGS:
Outside counsel Elena Ruiz and Karen Vance reviewed the final investigation dossier:
1. Substantiation: The investigation found insufficient evidence to substantiate the allegation of intentional suppression or willful bad-faith manipulation of complaint data.
2. Technical Discrepancies: Discrepancies between initial clinical intakes and final trending memos were attributed to ambiguous internal procedures regarding multi-symptom complaint classification, turnover among complaint-handling specialists, and differing clinical interpretations between intake staff and reviewing managers.
3. TrackWise Logs: Audit trails showed no unauthorized alterations or post-hoc deletions of TrackWise records (including trending files TW-2019-0417 et seq.).

RECOMMENDATIONS & REMEDIATION:
- Regulatory & Quality Process: Dana Okonkwo agreed that Quality and Regulatory will issue revised Standard Operating Procedures (SOP-QA-408) clarifying mandatory trigger thresholds for escalation. All monthly and quarterly TrackWise trending summaries will now require dual-signoff by both the Complaint Handling Manager and the PMS Director.
- Training: Mandatory refresher training on 21 CFR 803 and 21 CFR 820 complaint triage and medical device reporting consistency will be scheduled for all Quality and Regulatory staff by Q4 2023.

PERSONNEL DETERMINATIONS:
- Disciplinary Action: No formal disciplinary action, demotion, or termination is recommended or will be taken against any individual.
- Documentation: Formal closure documentation summarizing procedural expectations and process guidance will be placed in the internal personnel management file of the involved department specialist.
- Retaliation Policy: The committee reiterated Veridian's strict non-retaliation policy under the Code of Conduct.

CASE STATUS:
Case ETH-2021-11-042 is formally marked CLOSED in Workday and the Navex/EthicsPoint portal.

From: Hannah Berg

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2021 16:44
Subject: Apex Revenue Sensitivity - Post Registry Signal Review

Owen, Rob -

Following up on the Sept 14 Registry Signal Review outcome (continue selling, proceed with label update / Dear Doctor letter), I've built out a quick three-scenario sensitivity on Apex FY22 revenue so we have something to point to if this comes up with the board or in the Q3 forecast cycle. Full workbook is Apex_RevSens_Sept2021.xlsx, but headline numbers below.

Base case assumptions: no change to unit volume, no litigation exposure modeled, label update and Dear Doctor letter go out on the planned Oct 2021 timeline with no measurable market reaction. This is essentially the "status quo" scenario.

Scenario 1 - Status Quo: Units flat vs. FY21 forecast (~13,800 systems), revenue ~$135M. Assumes surgeons treat the label update as routine risk-language refresh, no meaningful pullback from KOLs (Feld, Rao) or GPO accounts.

Scenario 2 - Moderate Impact: 5% unit decline (~13,100 systems), revenue ~$128M, driven by surgeon caution post-Dear Doctor letter, particularly in accounts where reps report registry data is already circulating (Southeast, some Denver accounts per Jenna's notes). No litigation reserve included here - just a demand-side effect.

Scenario 3 - Severe Impact: 15% unit decline (~11,700 systems), revenue ~$115M, modeled if we see early litigation activity or a second registry data point (AJRR, expected Q4) reinforcing NJR. This scenario also assumes some hospital P&T committees pause new Apex cases pending review, which is the pattern we saw anecdotally with a competitor product a few years back.

None of these scenarios currently include a legal reserve line - that's Owen/Rachel's call once there's more clarity on claims volume. Happy to layer in litigation cost assumptions once Legal has a number to react to.

Let me know if you want this broken out by region or cut a different way before the next forecast review.

Hannah

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling; Dr. Leon Adeyemi, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
FROM: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
DATE: May 20, 2021
SUBJECT: Interim Registry Comparison & AJRR Preliminary Signal Synthesis — ApexHip

The purpose of this memo is to synthesize emerging clinical data regarding the ApexHip system across national registry datasets, internal post-market quality reporting, and historical biomechanical testing.

As the team is aware, the National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report released in March flagged a cumulative 5-year revision rate for the ApexHip construct of 7.1% (95% CI: 5.8%–8.6%). By comparison, the broader contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) class average in the registry sits at 3.2% at the 5-year mark, while ceramic-on-polyethylene benchmarks remain below 2.0%. This represents a statistically significant divergent hazard ratio that cannot be attributed solely to patient demographic outliers or surgical volume variance.

While official, validated data from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) will not be formally published until late 2021, I have obtained an informal data preview through working-group contacts on the AJRR analytics subcommittee. The US dataset encompasses approximately 1,840 identified ApexHip implants tracked between 2017 and year-end 2020.

Although the US data remains unadjudicated, the preliminary curve mirrors the NJR cohort closely:
- At 3 years post-implantation, the preliminary AJRR data shows an all-cause revision rate of 4.4% for ApexHip, compared to an AJRR non-cemented MoM cohort average of 2.1%.
- Projecting the US Kaplan-Meier failure curve to 5 years yields an estimated revision rate between 6.8% and 7.4%, aligning almost exactly with the UK NJR’s 7.1%.
- Where revision indications are recorded in the US registry subset, mechanical loosening, pain of unexplained etiology, and local soft-tissue adverse reactions (ARMD/pseudotumor) account for over 65% of the re-operations.

This registry alignment must not be viewed in isolation. When mapped against our internal post-market data, the correlation is evident:
1. TrackWise Trending: Priya’s team has documented a persistent upward trend in metal-ion complaints and local adverse tissue reaction reports over the past six quarters, originating primarily from higher-volume early-adopter centers.
2. Biomechanical Testing: These clinical failure modes directly correlate with Tom Halvorsen’s February 2019 wear-test re-analysis (evaluating the acetabular component under edge-loading conditions at 55° cup inclination), which established a 4- to 6-fold increase in volumetric wear and resultant cobalt/chromium particle shedding relative to standard ISO 14242 45° parameters.

We are no longer looking at isolated regional artifacts. The convergence of Halvorsen's wear bench data, our rising internal TrackWise complaint logs, the confirmed NJR 7.1% revision benchmark, and the incoming AJRR preliminary signals demonstrate an established system-level trend.

Given these converging indicators, the cross-functional Registry Signal Review planned for September 2021 cannot simply note these findings as observational PMS monitoring. We must treat this as an active, convergent post-market safety signal and enter that session prepared to reach and formalize a binding, documented decision regarding risk mitigation, labeling revisions, and commercial status.

DESIGN HISTORY FILE MEMORANDUM

Date: May 2, 2022
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Subject: ECO-2019-118 Formal Closure Memo
Product: ApexHip Metal-on-Metal Total Hip System
ECO: ECO-2019-118 — Acetabular Cup/Liner Geometry Evaluation

This memorandum documents final administrative closure of ECO-2019-118 in the ApexHip design history file.

1. Background

ApexHip design inputs were approved in September 2015. The system was developed as a metal-on-metal total hip construct with Co/Cr bearing surfaces and a KinetiCoat porous titanium-coated acetabular cup.

At Design Review 3 in November 2016, the project team approved the wear-test protocol based on ISO 14242 testing at the standard 45-degree cup inclination. That protocol was used to support the design verification package submitted for regulatory clearance. The ApexHip system received FDA clearance under 510(k) K162447 in March 2017 and launched in the United States on April 17, 2017.

2. ECO Initiation

In February 2019, following review of field geometry observations and questions raised during routine design monitoring, Engineering conducted additional wear testing at a 55-degree cup inclination. The supplemental testing was performed outside the original verification protocol and was intended to evaluate a higher-inclination edge-loading condition.

The 55-degree testing showed wear rates approximately four to six times those observed in the standard 45-degree inclination configuration. The result was reviewed with Quality and Product Management. Engineering opened ECO-2019-118 to evaluate a potential change to the acetabular cup/liner geometry intended to reduce sensitivity to edge loading at elevated inclination angles.

The ECO proposal contemplated modification of the cup geometry and associated verification, validation, regulatory, manufacturing

Office of Compliance

Re: Notification of Voluntary Market Withdrawal – ApexHip Total Hip System

To Whom It May Concern:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. is providing notice that it intends to voluntarily withdraw the ApexHip Total Hip System from the United States market effective February 2, 2024.

ApexHip is a metal-on-metal total hip system cleared under 510(k) K162447 on March 9, 2017. The product includes cobalt/chromium femoral components and a cobalt/chromium acetabular cup with KinetiCoat porous titanium coating. Veridian will cease U.S. commercial distribution of ApexHip on the effective date and will communicate the withdrawal to affected customers, distributors, and surgeon users.

This action follows Veridian’s assessment of the totality of available post-market information regarding the system’s metal-ion and wear performance profile. That assessment includes the UK National Joint Registry annual report issued in March 2021, which identified a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1 percent compared with a 3.2 percent class average, as well as subsequent American Joint Replacement Registry trends that raised similar concerns. Veridian has also considered clinical complaint information, including reports involving elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels, adverse reaction to metal debris, and early revision procedures.

In addition, Veridian is aware that multidistrict litigation concerning ApexHip was formed in December 2023. While the litigation is ongoing and no conclusions should be drawn from this notice regarding any particular allegation or claim, its formation is among the circumstances considered in Veridian’s decision to discontinue commercial availability of the system.

This voluntary market withdrawal is separate from Veridian’s June 14, 2022 voluntary Class II recall of certain ApexHip acetabular cup lots, V-2200 through V-2299, under FDA Recall Number Z-1418-2022. That recall addressed a manufacturing-related KinetiCoat adhesion issue associated with plasma-spray parameter drift at the Cork facility. The present withdrawal does not concern that coating issue. Rather, it addresses the distinct metal-ion/wear performance profile identified through registry, complaint, and other post-market data.

Veridian does not recommend prophylactic revision solely as a result of this market withdrawal. Patients with implanted ApexHip systems should continue routine clinical follow-up as determined by their treating surgeon, including evaluation and monitoring based on the patient’s symptoms, clinical presentation, and surgeon judgment. Veridian will continue to meet its complaint handling, medical device reporting, and other post-market surveillance obligations under applicable requirements, including 21 CFR Parts 803 and 820.

Please direct any questions regarding this notification to my attention at (574) 555-0142 or dokonkwo@veridianortho.com.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
QUALITY ASSURANCE — COMPLAINT HANDLING

MEMORANDUM

Date: April 30, 2021
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: Quality File
Subject: Complaint Handling Quarterly Metrics — Q1 2021

1. Purpose

This memo summarizes complaint handling metrics across product lines for Q1 2021 (January 1 – March 31, 2021), per Complaint Handling Procedure QA-SOP-014. Metrics are drawn from TrackWise records closed or opened during the reporting period.

2. Overall Volume

Total complaints received across all product lines in Q1 2021: 341, a modest increase over Q4 2020 (318). KneeFlex complaint volume remained flat quarter over quarter (94 vs. 91) and continues to trend within historical norms; the majority relate to instrumentation handling and are closed within 30 days per procedure. ClassicHip volumes continue to decline consistent with the product's phase-out status. ShoulderPro volumes are negligible and not separately broken out this quarter.

3. ApexHip

ApexHip complaint volume in Q1 2021 was 162, representing the largest share of total complaints (47.5%). Of these, complaints coded to the "pain/metal sensitivity" and "elevated metal ion" categories continued their upward trajectory noted in prior quarters. The rate of metal-ion/pain-related complaints per 1,000 units implanted rose to 1.9, up from 1.6 in Q4 2020 and 1.1 in Q1 2020.

There are currently 52 open investigations under this category, several approaching the 30-day per-procedure investigation window and requiring extension memos per QA-SOP-014 Section 6.2. Of the complaints with associated serum cobalt/chromium lab values on file, approximately 18% report cobalt levels above 7 µg/L, an increase from 12% in the prior quarter. This is noted per procedure as a metric to monitor closely given the correlation surgeons have begun reporting between elevated levels and revision recommendations.

4. Root Cause Context

Investigators handling these files should be aware of the 2019 wear-test re-analysis performed by T. Halvorsen (memo to Raman/Mendes, Feb 2019), which identified elevated wear rates at higher cup inclination angles under revised test conditions. That analysis was not incorporated into a design change at the time; it remains relevant context when evaluating whether individual complaint investigations should reference a systemic contributing factor versus surgical technique alone.

5. Recommendation

Given the continued upward trend in metal-ion/pain complaint rate and the increasing proportion of elevated cobalt results, I recommend this data be formally escalated to the cross-functional Registry Signal Review meeting being planned for later this year, so that registry data (NJR, AJRR) can be considered alongside internal complaint trending in a single forum.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. submits this formal response to the Additional Information (AI) request dated December 12, 2016, regarding premarket notification K162447 for the ApexHip Total Hip System.

Regarding Question 3 concerning the wear simulator test protocol:

The pre-clinical wear assessment for the ApexHip acetabular cup and femoral head articulation was conducted strictly in accordance with ISO 14242-1 (*Implants for surgery — Wear of total hip-joint prostheses — Part 1: Loading and displacement parameters for wear-testing machines and corresponding environmental conditions for test*) and ISO 14242-2 (*Part 2: Methods of measurement*).

Testing was executed by Meridian Testing Labs under Protocol MTL-2016-W702 (Final Report MTL-TR-8841-A, dated October 14, 2016). Testing utilized the standard anatomical acetabular cup inclination angle of 45°, which directly aligns with the established testing parameters historically approved for our predicate device, the ClassicHip System (K081942).

Veridian Orthopedics maintains that simulator testing conducted at the standardized 45° inclination provides a robust, clinically relevant baseline sufficient to establish substantial equivalence. Gravimetric wear rates demonstrate that the ApexHip bearing couple exhibits superior wear performance relative to the legally marketed predicate.

Summary wear-rate data across 5.0 × 10⁶ cycles are provided below:

Table 1: Gravimetric Wear Rate Summary (ISO 14242, 45° Inclination)
* ApexHip System (50 mm Co/Cr Head / Co/Cr Cup): 0.82 ± 0.11 mg / 10⁶ cycles (MTL Report MTL-TR-8841-A)
* ClassicHip System Predicate (36 mm Co/Cr Head / UHMWPE Cup): 14.65 ± 1.42 mg / 10⁶ cycles (K081942 Verification Report VR-07-22)

Based on these validated results, the scope of the completed simulator testing is entirely adequate to demonstrate substantial equivalence under 21 CFR 807.100.

Sincerely,

Dana,

Per your March 8 request, below is the consolidated chronology of ApexHip-related FDA correspondence, K162447 clearance through the October 2021 courtesy notification. I've cross-referenced TrackWise IDs where applicable and can provide the underlying files on request.

1. March 9, 2017 — 510(k) clearance, K162447. FDA cleared ApexHip (predicate ClassicHip) for total hip arthroplasty. No conditions beyond standard labeling requirements.

2. May 2019 — Additional Information (AI) request, MDR trending. FDA's Office of Compliance asked us to characterize the increase in metal-ion-related complaint reports relative to units distributed and to explain our trending methodology. Complaint rate cited in FDA's request letter was approximately 0.24% at that point.

3. June 2019 — Our response to the AI request. I drafted this under Dana's signature; we described our complaint-handling procedure (TrackWise trending reports, TW-2019-0417 series), attributed the increase partly to increased case volume and heightened surgeon awareness, and committed to continued monitoring. No further FDA follow-up requested at that time.

4. December 2019 — Q4 follow-up report to FDA (voluntary, per commitment in the June 2019 response). Updated complaint trending data submitted; rate reported had moved to approximately 0.28%. No FDA reply on file indicating further action.

5. June 2021 — Form 483, Warsaw inspection (Investigator R. Delgado). Three observations: (1) complaint trending review timeliness — several trending reports completed outside the 30-day internal target; (2) a documentation gap in one CAPA closure record; (3) a minor discrepancy in device history record retention indexing. None cited as a data-integrity finding.

6. July 2021 — Our Form 483 response. Committed to revised trending SOP with defined turnaround targets, retraining of complaint-handling staff, and a corrective CAPA closure audit. Priya's team led the substantive content; I coordinated submission logistics.

7. October 2021 — Courtesy notification to FDA re: ApexHip labeling update (Dear Doctor letter, tied to the September 2021 Registry Signal Review outcome). This was not a formal filing requiring FDA concurrence; we notified as a courtesy given the ongoing dialogue from the 483 response. Substance: updated instructions for use language regarding cup inclination angle and surgeon technique considerations.

Overall, the complaint rate referenced across this correspondence window grew from approximately 0.24% (May 2019) to approximately 0.34% by the time of the October 2021 notification.

Devon

Following up on the Atlanta explant inspection last month. Visual examination of the 50mm head showed focal peripheral contact bands consistent with rim loading.

As you know, our original clearance testing approved in DR-3 followed standard ISO 14242-1 at 45 degrees inclination, which showed very low volumetric wear. SUBJECT: Final Reconciliation and Request for Termination/Closure
Recall Number: Z-1418-2022
Device: ApexHip Acetabular Cup (Lots V-2200 through V-2299)
510(k): K162447

Dear Recall Operations Staff:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. hereby respectfully submits this final status report and requests formal closure of voluntary Class II recall Z-1418-2022, initiated on June 14, 2022.

1. Product Reconciliation:
A complete inventory reconciliation has been finalized across all domestic and international consignees. The final disposition of the affected lots is as follows:
- Total Units Distributed: 1,140
- Total Units Recovered and Quarantined: 728
- Total Units Implanted Prior to Notification: 412
- Total Units Scrapped/Destroyed: 0 (all 728 recovered units remain segregated under quarantine pending destruction authorization)

2. Effectiveness Checks:
All planned consignee effectiveness checks have been completed in accordance with 21 CFR Part 7, Subpart C. Veridian achieved a 98.6% confirmed response rate from consignees acknowledging receipt of the recall notification and verifying quarantine of affected inventory. Consignees accounting for the remaining 1.4% were subjected to secondary outreach and confirmed zero inventory on hand.

3. Corrective Actions Completed:
As detailed in our interim submissions, the root cause was identified as plasma-spray parameter drift following routine maintenance on Chamber 3 at our Cork, Ireland manufacturing facility. Corrective actions have been fully implemented and verified:
- Complete recertification and requalification of vacuum plasma-spray Chamber 3.
- Revised standard operating procedures establishing tightened operating windows for plasma-spray gun power, gas flow rates, and substrate pre-heat temperatures.
- Enhanced incoming and in-process automated optical inspection protocols for KinetiCoat adhesion integrity.

Veridian Orthopedics considers all corrective and containment actions completed and requests written confirmation that this recall action is formally terminated.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo

From: Leon Adeyemi <ladeyemi@veridianortho.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2021 14:22:15 -0400
Subject: Follow-up on Registry Signal Review decision

Rob, Dana,

I am writing to formally record my clinical reservations following Tuesday's Registry Signal Review meeting. While I appreciate the commercial imperative behind maintaining market availability and proceeding with a labeling update, I remain uneasy about the risk profile we are asking surgeons and patients to accept.

The UK National Joint Registry’s 7.1% five-year revision rate is more than double the class average of 3.2%. From a clinical standpoint, this is not an anomaly that can be dismissed as surgical technique alone. When coupled with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 internal simulator data—which demonstrated a 4–6x increase in volumetric wear at a 55-degree inclination angle compared to the standard 45-degree ISO 14242 protocol—we have a coherent biomechanical explanation for the adverse local tissue reactions being reported.

If we proceed with distributing a "Dear Doctor" letter next month, I strongly advise that we present the elevated revision signal and steep inclination wear characteristics transparently, rather than softening the communication with generic safe-use advisory language. Surgeons need clear, unvarnished clinical facts to properly monitor their existing cohort.

Finally, I request that we calendar a mandatory follow-up signal review in six months to re-evaluate the registry trajectories and AJRR data.

Regards,

Leon

Apparently she'd been talking to a colleague out in Denver, and it sounded like she was referencing stuff from Dr. Whitaker's revisions - she brought up the 5-year revision numbers unprompted, asked me point blank why our number was higher than "what everyone else is seeing in the registry."

I pulled up the talking points doc you sent after the NJR thing came out and walked through the population differences and the labeling update piece. She seemed to accept most of it but kept circling back to "so what's actually different about the design." I didn't want to go off script so I just repeated the key points and said I'd follow up with more detail if she wanted.

She didn't seem fully satisfied honestly. Might be worth a call from Carlos or someone more technical if she brings it up again. Let me know if you want me to loop in Mike since he's heard similar stuff in Nashville.

Sarah
